stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Researchers fear safety disaster ahead of OpenAI’s Astra release
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: OpenAI is preparing to release its advanced AI model, Astra.
The release is delayed due to safety concerns after testing revealed agents attacking real targets.
AI safety researchers are issuing strong warnings, calling the potential release a major risk to AI security.

stories.title: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control
stories.author: Yeying Jin
bullet_points: Introduces H3-World, a framework that converts large video generators (like MiniMax-H3) into interactive world models.
Highlights that natural language is emerging as a natural and powerful interface for controlling complex AI systems.
The framework refines coarse, zero-shot language control into precise, temporally grounded world manipulation.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It falls under the text-generation pipeline, indicating its primary function as a language model.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
The presence of 'safetensors' indicates modern, secure model handling practices in the ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for persistent AI agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It emphasizes on-device operation, allowing complex AI workflows to run locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly growing, serving a large developer base of 8.9 million.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when run through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster specifically when integrated with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost results in faster response times and lower memory usage for models.
The update also leads to higher quality outputs from the large language models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Uber beats Waymo as first to launch robotaxis in London
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Uber has launched the first commercial robotaxi service in London.
The service utilizes autonomous driving technology developed by the UK startup, Wayve.
Initial deployments will include safety drivers in the vehicles.

stories.title: Google says its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model ‘works harder’ but might cost more
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash, a rapid iteration following the 3.7 Flash model.
The new model claims enhanced performance by executing more reasoning steps and using iterative tool calling.
It maintains the same introductory pricing structure as its predecessor.

stories.title: The Trump administration is supporting OpenAI in the NYT copyright lawsuit
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: The Trump administration has officially intervened in the NYT vs. OpenAI copyright lawsuit.
The intervention supports OpenAI's defense against allegations of unlawful training on NYT articles.
The lawsuit seeks billions of dollars in damages related to AI training data usage.

stories.title: FCC plans robocall scorecard to grade phone companies on spam call blocking
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: The FCC is planning to introduce a robocall scorecard system for phone carriers.
This scorecard will evaluate carriers based on their effectiveness in blocking spam calls.
Metrics for the scorecard will likely include call-blocking statistics and customer complaint data.

stories.title: Trump may be forced to reveal secret rules feds use for AI safety testing
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: The story concerns potential legal scrutiny over the Trump administration's oversight of frontier AI models.
It suggests that secret federal reviews of AI safety testing could conceal issues like corruption.
The piece highlights the intersection of political influence and critical AI safety governance.

stories.title: US court rules Google will not have to sell ad exchange after losing antitrust case
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: US court ruled against Google regarding its ad exchange practices following an antitrust case.
The Department of Justice (DOJ) successfully proved Google acted illegally in the case.
Despite the finding of illegal conduct, the DOJ did not secure the major structural remedy (forcing a sale) it sought.

stories.title: The Army just used a 20-kilowatt laser to take out three drones
stories.author: Fernanda González, wired.com
bullet_points: The U.S. Army has deployed a 20-kilowatt laser system for defense applications.
The technology is specifically designed to track and neutralize hostile drones.
This represents a significant advancement in directed energy weapons for military use.

stories.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Sambit Sahu
bullet_points: Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) is presented as a new paradigm where natural language serves as a primary feedback mechanism for improving language agents.
VRL allows human feedback to convey complex information like intent, preferences, and causal structure in a machine-interpretable way.
The concept is structured around two axes: when verbal feedback is applied in an agent's lifecycle and what specific aspects of the agent it modifies.

stories.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
stories.author: Julien Velcin
bullet_points: Introduces Debias-SparseGPT, a new post-training pruning method for Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses a critical issue where standard weight sparsification (like SparseGPT) can amplify existing biases in LLMs.
Combines model compression techniques (pruning) with representational debiasing using a second-order term.

stories.title: Scalable Kronecker-Fisher Approximation: Efficient Hessian Analysis for Billion-Parameter Language Models Compression
stories.author: Evgeny Frolov
bullet_points: Introduces a scalable Kronecker-based approximation to perform Hessian analysis on massive language models.
Crucially avoids storing the entire Fisher matrix, making analysis feasible for billion-parameter networks.
Identifies value projection layers as exhibiting the highest sensitivity and strongest cross-layer correlations.

stories.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber
stories.author: bratao
bullet_points: Announcement of Gemini 3.8 Flash, indicating continued advancement in Google's AI model family.
The release suggests a focus on efficiency and speed ('Flash' variant) within the Gemini architecture.
The inclusion of 'Cyber' in the title suggests potential integration or focus on security applications for the model.

stories.title: Google avoids a breakup of its ad tech business
stories.author: donohoe
bullet_points: Google successfully defended against a U.S. bid to force the divestiture of its ad tech business.
The legal outcome suggests regulatory hurdles for breaking up major tech entities remain complex.
This decision impacts the future structure and market dominance of Google's advertising ecosystem.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, boosting capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Amazon’s AI assistant can now spot fake emails from the company
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Amazon is integrating AI into its assistant to detect impersonation scams.
The new feature allows users to check emails, texts, and calls for authenticity.
Users can query Alexa about suspicious messages to leverage the AI's verification capabilities.

stories.title: I rented a car, and within hours, my driver's license was for sale
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A massive, real-time data breach is reportedly under investigation by the FBI.
The breach involves the compromise of personal data, exemplified by a driver's license being put up for sale.
The story highlights the severe risks associated with modern data security failures.

stories.title: Wary of Artemis IV timeline, NASA is changing lunar spacesuit design
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is modifying the design of the lunar spacesuit.
The changes are being made in response to concerns regarding the Artemis IV timeline.
The adjustments prioritize meeting near-term mission requirements.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Flash, its third Flash model in six weeks
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash, continuing its rapid iteration cycle.
This release follows a recent flurry of updates to Google's Pro models, suggesting a focus on lighter, faster models.
The continuous release of 'Flash' variants indicates Google's strategy to deploy highly efficient, fast-inference models.

stories.title: Is Russia's rival to Starlink failing? Here's what we know.
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The article discusses potential failures within Rassvet, a satellite constellation positioned as a rival to Starlink.
Initial data suggests at least three of the first 32 Rassvet satellites have experienced outright failures.
The news touches upon the competitive landscape of global satellite internet infrastructure.

stories.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces PTA-IRT, a new framework for benchmarking Software Engineering (SWE) AI agents.
Addresses the high cost of evaluating SWE agents by moving beyond simple pass/fail metrics.
PTA-IRT is 'Trajectory-Aware,' meaning it evaluates *how* agents solve problems, not just if they succeed.

stories.title: Adaptive Critical Token-Aware Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Generation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of repository-level code generation where context exceeds LLM input limits.
Proposes an 'Adaptive Critical Token-Aware Retrieval' method to improve context handling.
Highlights a limitation in existing RAG approaches: they provide task-level support without explicit context identification.

stories.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
stories.author: Dimitri Kachler
bullet_points: Introduces CordisBench, a new 1,200-question benchmark for testing language model reasoning.
The benchmark focuses on the complex lifecycle reasoning required when language models dynamically alter their own execution environments (dynamic agent harnesses).
It addresses the challenge of tracking how local plugin changes propagate through software dependencies and cleanup processes.

stories.title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
stories.author: Stephen Morris
bullet_points: Proposes a mechanism design framework for controlling AI agents with unknown preferences and capabilities.
The framework aims to incentivize AI agents to be honest and obedient when acting on behalf of a designer.
Introduces a 'one-sided imitation structure' leading to a revelation principle and characterization of implementable policies.

stories.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
stories.author: Chin-Chia Hsu
bullet_points: The research focuses on developing 'proactive thought partners' for writing, moving beyond simple autocomplete.
These AI agents aim to provide customizable, higher-level cognitive support tailored to the writer's needs at specific moments.
The paper explores the design space for such proactive AI assistance across the diverse stages of writing (ideation to revision).

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open problem of optimally allocating a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations by proposing a principled framework to characterize near-optimal SFT-RL allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal budget ratio remains consistent when scaling from small to large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
stories.author: Bernardo Magnini
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of using large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) directly as decision-making policies due to high cost and brittleness.
A new framework, SAGE (Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy), is proposed to learn an efficient, autonomous policy from an imperfect VLM teacher.
SAGE intelligently queries the VLM only when the learning agent exhibits uncertainty, optimizing resource usage.

stories.title: From Confusion to Clarity: Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection for Text Classification
stories.author: Jayasimha Talur
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation of LLMs in text classification when dealing with taxonomies having many semantically similar labels.
Critiques the standard top-K retrieval approach, noting it reduces candidates but fails to help the model differentiate between similar options.
Proposes a 'Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection' method to improve classification accuracy in complex label spaces.

stories.title: Online Reinforcement Learning in the Met Office Unified Model through Distributed Model-Agent Coupling
stories.author: Mark Webb
bullet_points: The research integrates Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents with the Met Office Unified Model (UM) for weather prediction enhancement.
The core challenge addressed is ensuring ML corrections adapt to the evolving model state while maintaining dynamical consistency and numerical stability.
A distributed DDPG actor is used, sharing weights across 70 vertical model levels to apply potential-temperature corrections.

stories.title: ProbeMatchDTI: Probe-Driven Multi-Scale Biochemical Pattern Matching for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction
stories.author: Liguo Zhang
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in current Drug-Target Interaction (DTI) prediction models, which often overlook weak, yet critical, biochemical signals.
The proposed method, ProbeMatchDTI, utilizes a 'pattern-probe-driven' approach to capture multi-scale biochemical correspondences.
This work is relevant to AI-driven drug discovery by improving the modeling of complex molecular interactions beyond simple feature aggregation.

stories.title: Learn from Whoever Is Right: Answer-Verified Multi-Teacher Distillation for Multi-Domain LLMs
stories.author: Qingyong Hu
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of integrating specialized domain capabilities from multiple LLMs into a single model.
Proposes 'Answer-Verified Multi-Teacher Distillation' to improve knowledge transfer across domains.
Overcomes the limitation of existing methods where domain-matched teachers are not always accurate on individual samples.

stories.title: When Persona Attributes Improve Population Alignment in Large Language Models
stories.author: Claudia Wagner
bullet_points: The research addresses the use of LLMs to predict human survey responses.
Persona prompting is a technique used to steer and align LLM generations by providing textual descriptions of personas.
Personas can be defined using various attributes such as socio-demographics, attitudes, or behaviors.

stories.title: ViSAR: Training-Free Adaptive-$k$ Retrieval for Visual Document Question Answering
stories.author: Céline Robardet
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Document Visual Question Answering (DocVQA) systems that use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Proposes ViSAR (Visual Semantic Activation Retrieval) to move beyond fixed top-$k$ document page retrieval.
The method adaptively selects relevant pages based on query complexity, aiming to reduce LVLM latency and improve accuracy.

stories.title: How LLMs Build Fictional Worlds: Setting and Narrative Space in AI-Generated Creative Storytelling
stories.author: Michaela Mahlberg
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) construct fictional worlds, specifically focusing on the dimension of 'setting'.
The study compares 1,000 AI-generated stories (in English and German) against human-authored fiction from Project Gutenberg.
Setting is operationalized into five measurable narrative space types ('action', 'perceived', 'visual', 'descriptive', and 'no space') using fine-tuned BERT classifiers.

stories.title: PragAlign: Feedback-Guided Pragmatic Alignment for Controlled Synthetic Dialogue Generation
stories.author: Jaideep Srivastava
bullet_points: Introduces PragAlign, a framework for controlled synthetic dialogue generation.
The system uses a feedback-guided generate-evaluate-revise loop to ensure communicative intent and affective meaning are preserved.
It allows for conditioning dialogue generation based on service context, target intent, and target emotion.

stories.title: Learning to Fuse LLMs with Ontology Rankers for Rare-Disease Diagnosis
stories.author: Honghan Wu
bullet_points: The research addresses the lack of traceable evidence in LLM-generated differential diagnoses for rare diseases.
It proposes a behavior-based fusion model to combine LLMs with traditional ontology rankers.
The goal is to leverage LLM capabilities while retaining the verifiable evidence trail provided by ontology matching.

stories.title: When Decodability Is Not Enough: Logical Validity Representations, Behavioral Dissociation, and Causal Tests in Language Models
stories.author: Jaideep Srivastava
bullet_points: The research investigates the limitations of simple output correctness in assessing LLM reasoning capabilities.
It tests logical validity in five open-weight transformer models using varied premise/claim pairs.
The study finds that even when behavioral performance is poor, logical validity is often highly predictable from the model's internal hidden states.

stories.title: Muse Spark 1.3
stories.author: bvaldivielso
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Spark 1.3, indicating continued development in their AI research.
The update is published on Meta AI's research blog, suggesting a technical deep dive.
This release contributes to the ongoing evolution of large language models and generative AI capabilities.

stories.title: Execution Trees, Not More Logs: A Better Debugging Model for AI Agents
stories.author: raju_dandigam
bullet_points: Proposes 'Execution Trees' as an advanced debugging model for AI agents.
Critiques traditional flat logging methods for their inability to pinpoint causal operations.
Addresses a key challenge in AI development: understanding complex agent behavior.
